Summary: Aircraft-level interface contracts shall be versioned and published for propulsion, flight controls, ECS, landing gear, and vision.
Interface contracts shall define units, sign conventions, rates, tolerances, and timeout semantics.
Mechanical interface contracts shall define mounting datums and load directions.
Electrical interface contracts shall define nominal voltage ranges and fault annunciation channels.
The design process shall allow at least two viable propulsion architectures until evidence eliminates one.
Major architecture decisions shall document rationale, assumptions, and confidence level.
A subsystem may not be declared integrated unless all required interface fields are mapped and verified.
Integration assumptions shall be traceable to a requirement or explicit open issue.
The repository shall define and maintain one controlled baseline aircraft configuration at all times.
The baseline configuration shall include target MTOW, empty weight estimate, CG envelope, and margin assumptions.
All subsystem packaging volumes (FCS, ICE, MOTOR, ECS, GEAR, VISION) shall be represented in the baseline geometry.
Baseline geometry changes that affect subsystem interfaces shall include an impact note.
Each baseline release shall include updated mass and CG calculations.
Each baseline release shall include an interface consistency check across subsystem repos.
Requirement-to-evidence traceability shall be maintained for all aircraft-level requirements.
Unverified assumptions shall be listed in an open assumptions register.
The controller shall detect out-of-range pressure, out-of-range temperature, and sensor plausibility faults.
Fault handling shall define degraded thermal operation and safe shutdown triggers.
Pressurization-related faults shall generate explicit high-priority alerts.
Fault transitions shall be logged with timestamp and reason code.
Electrical interface shall define steady-state power budget, startup behavior, and fault boundaries.
Air/duct interface shall define flow assumptions, pressure-drop assumptions, and mechanical connection constraints.
Thermal interface shall define temperature sensing points and allowable control bands.
Control interface shall define command rates, telemetry rates, and timeout/fallback behavior.
The ECS subsystem shall provide controllable cabin thermal conditioning for baseline flight operations.
The architecture shall preserve a defined upgrade path to controlled pressurization.
The controller shall support mode states for off, thermal-control, and pressurization-development modes.
The subsystem shall expose commanded mode and measured mode state.
Simulation shall cover representative thermal load cases for climb, cruise, and descent.
Bench testing shall verify control-loop behavior and sensor fault handling.
Pressurization development logic shall be validated in a controlled non-flight test setup before integration.
Requirement traceability to test evidence shall be maintained.
The system shall support triplex FCC operation with deterministic lane health publication.
The voter shall support triplex and degraded duplex operation modes.
The control stack shall support normal, degraded, and fail-safe mode declarations.
Control outputs shall be deterministic for a given input/state set.
The subsystem shall detect steering command loss, brake command loss, and position-sensing faults.
Fault responses shall define safe degraded ground-handling behavior.
Critical gear faults shall generate explicit alerts and event logs.
Fault transitions shall be deterministic and traceable.
Mechanical interfaces shall define mount locations, load paths, and tolerance assumptions.
Steering/braking command interfaces shall define units, rates, and timeout behavior.
If powered actuation is used, electrical/hydraulic interfaces shall define nominal ranges and fault flags.
Gear status telemetry shall include position state, brake state, and detected fault state.
Landing gear architecture shall support taxi, takeoff, landing, and rollout loads defined by the baseline aircraft assumptions.
The subsystem shall define operating limits for speed, sink rate, and side-load assumptions.
Steering and braking interfaces shall be defined for baseline operations and degraded operation.
Gear subsystem status shall be available to other subsystems via normalized telemetry.
Static load cases shall be analyzed and documented against baseline assumptions.
Kinematic travel and interference checks shall be performed for nominal operation.
Steering and braking interface behaviors shall be bench-tested where applicable.
Requirement-to-evidence traceability shall be maintained.
The controller shall detect overtemp, overspeed, low oil pressure, and sensor plausibility faults.
Fault handling shall define degraded operation and commanded shutdown conditions.
Fault transitions shall be logged with timestamp and reason code.
Sensor loss shall not cause undefined controller outputs.
Mechanical coupling interface shall define shaft speed range, torque limits, and alignment tolerances.
Electrical interface shall define starter/generator power budgets and grounding constraints.
Thermal interface shall define coolant flow, temperature limits, and alarm thresholds.
Fuel interface shall define pressure, flow, and contamination assumptions.
Telemetry interface shall define units, update rates, and fault flags for FCS and logging tools.
The ICE subsystem shall support continuous generator-duty operation in the 100-230 kW target class.
The ICE subsystem shall publish commanded operating state and measured operating state each control cycle.
The ICE controller shall support startup, run, derate, and shutdown states with deterministic transitions.
The subsystem shall provide a configurable operating-point scheduler for efficiency-focused generator operation.
Bench tests shall cover startup, steady-state load steps, and commanded shutdown.
Bench tests shall include injected sensor fault scenarios and expected responses.
At least one requirement-mapped simulation campaign shall validate operating-point logic.
Requirements shall be traceable to test artifacts or open gaps.
The subsystem shall detect overcurrent, overvoltage, undervoltage, overtemperature, and comms timeout faults.
Fault responses shall be deterministic and include bounded torque reduction or controlled disable.
Fault behavior shall be role-aware (generator vs propulsor).
Fault and derating events shall be logged with reason codes.
HV bus interface shall define nominal voltage range, current limits, and inrush behavior.
Mechanical interface shall define shaft speed envelope, torque limits, and coupling assumptions.
Thermal interface shall define coolant requirements and derating thresholds.
Telemetry interface shall publish current, voltage, temperature, speed, torque estimate, and fault flags.
Control interface shall define command/update rates, timeout behavior, and fallback response.
The motor subsystem shall support propulsion operation in the 120-350 kW class through configurable hardware profiles.
The subsystem shall support both generator-role and propulsor-role configuration modes.
The motor controller shall implement deterministic state transitions for init, ready, run, derate, and fault.
Torque/speed command semantics shall be normalized independent of vendor-specific APIs.
Bench tests shall verify command-response behavior across the defined operating envelope.
Bench tests shall verify thermal derating behavior against configured thresholds.
Fault-injection tests shall verify each required protection path.
Requirement-to-test traceability shall be maintained.
The subsystem shall detect stale frames, stream dropout, and synchronization faults.
Degraded mode shall preserve usable pilot cues when possible.
Fault annunciation shall include clear state indication to the pilot/operator.
Fault events and mode transitions shall be logged with reason codes.
Sensor interface contracts shall define frame rate, resolution, timestamping, and synchronization assumptions.
Transport interface contracts shall define packet-loss behavior and latency/jitter budgets.
Display interface contracts shall define update rate, stale-frame indication, and degradation cues.
Control interface shall define command semantics for view selection and display mode changes.
The vision subsystem shall provide outside-scene presentation for pilot awareness using external camera feeds.
The subsystem shall support configurable camera profiles for different aircraft configurations.
The vision pipeline shall expose deterministic mode states (init, run, degraded, fault).
The system shall support fallback behavior when one or more camera streams are unavailable.
Latency and jitter measurements shall be validated against configured budgets.
Fault-injection scenarios shall include camera dropout, frozen frame, and transport loss.
Scenario-based tests shall evaluate degraded visibility handling.
Requirement-to-test traceability shall be maintained.
